variant.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet), and every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin.
The patient cases were chosen to cover a diverse range of conditions.

The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders, and a separate bias test that compares agent accuracy across patient demographic groups.

The agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at run time: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox, and they are not published in the repository.

Environment components are fixed at release: database snapshot, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are each version-pinned. During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.
To confirm that every task is solvable, we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct.
The grader checks whether the final answer matches the expected value.
A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.
We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%.
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times; this repeated-run policy is described in the main text.
We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores and test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02).
Headline scores carry 95% bootstrap CIs where the resampling unit is the task. When multiple tasks share a patient, the bootstrap resamples patients to address within-patient clustering.

To measure reliability, we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs, together with the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs.

Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types. The documentation states for every tool whether it only reads or also writes state, and describes what each tool returns, including the error message returned for invalid arguments. These tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt.

A table enumerates write actions affecting patient state: orders, notes, and messages. These execute on a sandboxed record copy. Scores penalize unnecessary or unsafe writes. The agent prompt discloses sandboxing.

Web access is blocked during runs; retrieval is confined to the task environment, preventing answer leakage through search. A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces. Released tasks include a canary string.
Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race), with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables.

The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database. Their use was approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method, and the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.
